# Integration Checklists — credential-gated work

- **🟡 0. Redis restore** — downgraded from 🔴 on 2026-08-04: login is no longer unprotected while Redis is down. See below.
- **A. Omise/Opn payments** — unblocks FC-11b (self-serve billing). Decision: [ADR-085]. Model: [ADR-084].
- **B. Push notifications** — unblocks the FC-13 push slice. Design: FEAT-023 (native_expo).

Two of the three (A, B) are fully designed but blocked only on external credentials — when
the keys arrive, follow the matching checklist; the data models/webhook/app scaffold are
already in place, so each is a "populate + wire + verify" job, not a redesign.

---

## 🟡 0. Redis restore

**Status (2026-08-04):** the login limiter no longer depends on Redis being up. When Redis is
unreachable `checkLoginRateLimit` now counts attempts in an **in-process fallback** instead of
waving everything through, and returns `degraded: true` so the state is visible. Brute-force
protection is therefore **enforced at all times** — just with a weaker ceiling while degraded
(5 × warm instances instead of a clean 5, because serverless instances do not share memory).

Restoring Redis is still worth doing (accurate limits + the app-wide `getOrSet` cache), but it
is no longer a security hole waiting on a credential.

**Previous status, for context:** from 2026-07-20 the limiter was hotfixed to return
`allowed: true` unconditionally on any Redis problem, which left login brute-force protection
off entirely for 15 days.

**What happened:** the Upstash Redis instance backing `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` /
`UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` was found to be **deleted** (`fetch failed` / DNS `ENOTFOUND`
for the configured host). Because the login rate-limiter was originally **fail-closed**
(by design, to resist brute force), every login attempt for every tenant threw and failed
— app-wide — from at least 2026-07-13 until diagnosed on 2026-07-20. (A secondary bug was
also found and fixed in the same incident: `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`'s stored value had a
literal `\r\n` text suffix corrupting it — that's fixed, but the underlying Redis
**database itself no longer exists**, which is the real blocker.)

### Checklist
- [ ] **Provision a working Upstash Redis database.** Either:
  - Vercel Dashboard → Project `zuri1.0` → **Storage** tab → add an Upstash/KV integration (auto-populates env vars), or
  - Create one directly in the [Upstash dashboard](https://console.upstash.com) and copy its REST URL + token.
- [ ] **Set `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`** on Vercel (Production **and** Preview environments) to the new database's values. Double-check for stray whitespace/control characters when pasting (this is exactly how the `\r\n` corruption happened) — verify with `vercel env pull` + `cat -A` before trusting a paste.
- [ ] **Verify connectivity** before relying on it: `curl <REST_URL>/ping -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"` should return `{"result":"PONG"}`, not a DNS/connection error.
- [ ] **Redeploy** (`vercel redeploy <latest-prod-deployment>` or push any commit) so the new env vars are picked up — Vercel does not hot-reload env vars into already-running functions.
- [x] ~~**Revert `checkLoginRateLimit` to fail-closed**~~ — done 2026-08-04, but **not** by restoring the original `throw`. Throwing is precisely what turned a dead Redis instance into an app-wide login outage; reverting to it would re-arm the same incident. The function now falls back to an in-process counter, so it enforces the limit without ever throwing. Nothing left to do here once Redis is back — it resumes using Redis automatically and `degraded` returns to `false`.
- [ ] **Sanity-check the general cache path too** — `src/lib/redis.js`'s `getOrSet` is fail-open by design (safe), but confirm the `[Redis] 'get'/'set' failed` warnings stop appearing in Vercel runtime logs (`get_runtime_errors`) after the fix, confirming the new instance is actually reachable app-wide (tenant-config cache, other `getOrSet` call sites).
- [ ] **Confirm `degraded: false`** — after the redeploy, the `[RateLimit] Redis … falling back to the per-instance counter` lines should stop appearing in runtime logs. That is the signal Redis is genuinely back, not just configured.
- [x] ~~Re-run `src/lib/rateLimit.test.js`~~ — rewritten 2026-08-04. It now asserts (a) the limiter never throws whatever Redis does, and (b) the 6th attempt is still refused when Redis is missing or erroring. Both incidents are pinned by tests.

## A. Omise/Opn payments (FC-11b)

**Blocked on:** an Omise/Opn account with test + live keys, **MIT (merchant-initiated) recurring enabled** in the agreement, and PromptPay enabled.

**What already exists (do NOT rebuild):**
- Data model: `Subscription`, `BillingEvent`, `PaymentMethod` (all `provider*` columns nullable) — `prisma/schema.prisma`.
- Repo: `src/lib/repositories/billingRepo.js` — `getBillingOverview`, `upsertSubscription`, `recordBillingEvent` (idempotent on `(provider, providerEventId)`).
- Webhook: `src/app/api/webhooks/billing/route.js` — already verifies Stripe-style + shared-secret signatures, resolves plan from priceId, flips `Tenant.plan`, and records Subscription + BillingEvent (non-fatal).
- Plan catalog: `src/lib/billing/plans.js` — `priceFor(plan, interval)` (THB; annual = 10× monthly).
- Read UI: `GET /api/settings/billing` + the Billing tab in `src/app/(dashboard)/settings/page.jsx` (currently shows a "contact support to change plan" note to replace).
- Gating: already active — `session.user.plan` populated in the NextAuth callbacks (auth-config.js) and enforced by `withAuth`.

### Checklist
- [ ] **Env / secrets:** `OMISE_SECRET_KEY` (server), `OMISE_PUBLIC_KEY` (client tokenization). Reuse `BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for the webhook. Never ship the secret key to the client.
- [ ] **Install:** server `omise` SDK; web client **Omise.js** (hosted card fields — keeps card data off our servers → **PCI-DSS SAQ-A**).
- [ ] **Card capture** (web Settings → Billing): Omise.js hosted fields → one-time token → server creates an Omise **customer** + attaches the card → store a `PaymentMethod` row with **only** `provider='omise'`, `providerPaymentMethodId`, `brand`, `last4`, `expMonth/expYear`. **Never** persist PAN/CVV. New route: `POST /api/settings/billing/payment-method` (withAuth `accounting:F`).
- [ ] **Subscribe / charge:** map plan → price via `priceFor(plan, interval)`; create the Omise schedule/charge on the saved card (MIT). Persist via `billingRepo.upsertSubscription(tenantId, { plan, status:'ACTIVE', interval, amount, provider:'omise', providerCustomerId, providerSubscriptionId, currentPeriodStart/End })`.
- [ ] **Webhook:** point the Omise webhook at the existing `POST /api/webhooks/billing`. Map Omise events → the existing handler: `charge.complete`/`charge.create` → `CHARGE` BillingEvent + plan flip; refund → `REFUND`. Idempotency is already handled via `(provider, providerEventId)` — pass Omise's event id as `providerEventId`.
- [ ] **Dunning (WE own it — Omise won't):** on a failed charge → set `Subscription.status='PAST_DUE'` + a retry schedule; after a grace period, downgrade to FREE (update **both** `Tenant.plan` and the Subscription). Nudge the owner in-app / on LINE. Build on the `Subscription.status` + `BillingEvent` (status `FAILED`) already in the model.
- [ ] **Self-serve upgrade/downgrade UI:** replace the "contact support" note in the Billing tab with a plan picker → confirm → charge. Downgrade at period end (`cancelAtPeriodEnd`), upgrade immediately (proration is our logic).
- [ ] **Plan-change propagation:** `Tenant.plan` gating is a JWT snapshot — a paid upgrade takes effect on next login. Bust the tenant cache in the webhook (like `tenantRepo.updateTenantConfig` does) and decide whether to force a token refresh so a fresh upgrade is felt promptly.
- [ ] **Verify (test mode):** (1) save a test card → `PaymentMethod` shows brand/last4; (2) subscribe → `BillingEvent` CHARGE recorded, `Tenant.plan` flips, gating grants the tier's routes; (3) failed test card → `PAST_DUE` + dunning fires; (4) PromptPay first payment renders its QR.
- [ ] **Compliance:** PCI SAQ-A (hosted fields/tokens only, never log tokens); PDPA for billing PII.

**Structural constraint to respect:** auto-renew = **MIT card charge**; PromptPay is a one-time QR (cannot be silently auto-billed monthly). PromptPay tenants without a saved card need a manual "pay invoice" re-scan each cycle — make that flow explicit in the UI. (See ADR-085.)

## B. Push notifications (FC-13)

**Blocked on:** an Expo/EAS project (`projectId`) + **FCM** credentials (Android, `google-services`) and **APNs** credentials (iOS key/cert) configured in EAS.

**Current state (mostly greenfield on the send side):**
- `WebPushSubscription` (`prisma/schema.prisma`) is **W3C web-push** shape (`endpoint`/`p256dh`/`auth`) — it does **not** fit an Expo push token. `src/lib/repositories/pushRepo.js` only stores/deactivates subscriptions.
- **There is no push *sender* anywhere** (no web-push, no expo-server-sdk). Nothing sends notifications today.
- The mobile app (`mobile/`) has **no** `expo-notifications` / `expo-device` deps and no notifications plugin in `app.json`.

### Checklist

**Schema**
- [ ] Add a dedicated **`PushDevice`** model (cleaner than overloading the web-push model): `{ id, tenantId, userId, expoToken @unique, platform ('ios'|'android'), isActive, createdAt, updatedAt }` + `@@index([tenantId])` + Tenant back-relation. Additive migration (ADR-078: include the migration file).

**Mobile (`mobile/`)**
- [ ] Add deps: `expo-notifications`, `expo-device`. In `app.json`: add the `expo-notifications` plugin and `extra.eas.projectId`.
- [ ] On app start (after login), request permission → `Notifications.getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` → `POST /api/push/register` (Bearer auth already works). On `logout()`, deactivate the token (call a `POST /api/push/unregister`, alongside the existing `mobile-logout`).
- [ ] Handle notification tap (`addNotificationResponseReceivedListener`) → route via `data` (e.g. `{ type:'message', conversationId }` → `/conversation/[id]`; `{ type:'task' }` → `/tasks`).

**Backend**
- [ ] Register endpoint: `POST /api/push/register` (withAuth) → upsert `PushDevice` by `expoToken`. `POST /api/push/unregister` → deactivate.
- [ ] Sender: install `expo-server-sdk`; `src/lib/push/expoPush.js` → `sendExpoPush(tenantId, userIds|'all', { title, body, data })`. Chunk messages, read receipts, and **deactivate tokens that come back `DeviceNotRegistered`**.
- [ ] Wire triggers on the events that already fire Pusher (`src/lib/pusher.js` call sites): `new-message` → the conversation's assignee/managers; `ai-order-requires-approval`; `agent-mode-escalated`; task assigned. Prefer the existing worker/trigger points.
- [ ] **Honor opt-in (FC-11a):** each user has `Employee.notificationPrefs` (per-event × per-channel, from `src/lib/settings/notificationPrefs.js`). Add/lean on a `push`/`inapp` channel and only send events the user enabled — don't spam.

**Verify**
- [ ] Push delivery needs a **real device** (iOS especially — the simulator won't receive real pushes). Register token → trigger an event → receive the notification → tap routes to the right screen.
- [ ] Invalid-token cleanup: uninstall/permission-revoke → next send marks the `PushDevice` inactive.

## Related follow-ups (not credential-blocked, but adjacent)
- **POS payment/settle** (FC-13) — pay an open order → PromptPay/cash/card + receipt. Overlaps with the Omise work (PromptPay) once keys exist.
- ~~**`guestCount` gap**~~ ✅ FIXED (C5): `POST /api/pos/orders` now validates + forwards `guestCount` (`OrderCreateSchema` + handler → `orderRepo.createOrder`, which already applied it). Remaining nicety: surface a guest-count input in the mobile new-order screen (`mobile/app/order/new/[tableId].jsx`) — the backend accepts it now.
- **Codegen drift (flagged during C5):** `src/app/api/pos/orders/route.js` is marked AUTO-GENERATED but has been hand-maintained (RMD-C02 atomic tx + C5) and diverges from `_outputs/T3.out.js`. Running `msp:compose FEAT-006-orders` would revert those fixes — reconcile `T3.out.js` before ever re-composing, or retire the codegen for this route.
